learned: The US Barista Express has one CLEAN / DESCALE light for both jobs: flashing means a cleaning (back-flush) cycle is due, solid means descale. Breville says the cleaning cycle 'is separate from descaling' (barista-express/clean-descale-light-us)

US Express cleaning cycle: put the 1 CUP basket, the cleaning disc and one tablet in the portafilter. With the machine off, hold 1 CUP + 2 CUP + POWER for about 10 s. The cycle runs about 5 minutes and ends with 2 beeps. Repeat it if the tablet hasn't dissolved (barista-express/cleaning-cycle-procedure-us)

US Express descale: dissolve one sachet in 1 L of water, then hold 2-CUP and POWER to enter Descale mode. Descale the coffee, steam and hot water components, repeat until the tank is empty, then rinse with a full 2 L tank (barista-express/descale-procedure-us)

The UK Sage Barista Express guide (SES875, C21) labels the light CLEAN ME, for cleaning only. It says the machine 'will not automatically prompt a reminder' for descaling and recommends descaling every 90 days at water hardness 4 or every 60 days at level 6. A post for both markets has to handle both panels (barista-express/clean-me-light-and-descale-interval-gb)

Breville lists 'machine needs to be descaled' as a cause of no water flow, espresso only dripping, no steam, and coffee not hot enough. It says scale reduces brewing flow, temperature, the power of the machine and taste. These are the symptoms that look like a fault but may be overdue descaling (barista-express/descale-symptoms-us, barista-pro/descale-symptoms)

Water filter: the US Express booklet says replace it every two months, more often in hard water, and remove it if you use filtered or bottled water (barista-express/water-filter-interval-us). The UK Express guide says every 3 months or 40 L, 60 L at hardness level 2 (barista-express/clean-me-light-and-descale-interval-gb)

Barista Pro US booklet: replace the filter every 2 months, more often in hard water (barista-pro/water-filter-interval-us). The Sage BES878/SES878 guide says every 3 months (barista-pro/water-filter-interval-sage). Breville says scale builds up even with the filter in place (barista-pro/filter-does-not-replace-descale)

The Barista Pro has no light. Its LCD shows a FLUSH alert for the cleaning cycle and a DESCALE alert for descaling, both started from the MENU. Descaling runs 3 stages (coffee, hot water, steam), then a 3-stage rinse (barista-pro/flush-alert-cleaning-cycle, barista-pro/descale-alert-procedure)
A brand-new Barista Pro also shows FLUSH for its first-use cycle, so a new owner can see FLUSH without any cleaning being due (barista-pro/first-use-flush)

Daily care is the same on both machines: wipe and purge the steam wand after milk, rinse the baskets and portafilter after use, wipe the group head and shower screen, purge the group, empty the drip tray, and hand-wash parts (no dishwasher). Soak blocked baskets in a dissolved cleaning tablet for about 20 minutes (barista-express/daily-care-us, barista-pro/daily-care)

On the Express, the silicone seal around the shower screen 'will need to be replaced' over time, using the included Allen key. Leaking around the portafilter edge or water leaking are the troubleshooting cues (barista-express/shower-seal-replacement)
The Barista Pro US booklet warns against alkaline cleaning agents and highly filtered, demineralised or distilled water (barista-pro/cleaning-cautions)

Owner evidence on the confusion: one Australian owner read a solid light as a backflush reminder for about two years. Other commenters disagreed about what it meant. The light went off only after the owner ran both a cleaning and a descale cycle (barista-express/owner-solid-light-confusion)
unknowns: No Breville or Sage source gives a shot count or calendar interval for the cleaning (back-flush) cycle on either machine, or for descaling the US Express or either Pro. Both are alert-driven. Breville's tutorial FAQs ('maintenance light is blinking/solid', 'How often does Barista Pro need descaling') had no answer text. A '3 months or 300 coffees' figure attributed to a manual was not found in any booklet read (barista-express/maintenance-interval-not-stated, barista-pro/maintenance-interval-not-stated)

How the Express light is triggered (shot counter, water volume or time) and how it resets: the US booklet gives no reset step. An owner says it is 'time or cycle based', which is unverified (barista-express/light-trigger-and-reset)
Whether current UK Sage Barista Express units still have a cleaning-only CLEAN ME light or now have the US-style CLEAN / DESCALE light: only the C21 quick guide was read

No replacement interval is given for the shower-screen seal on either machine. The Barista Pro US booklet and the Sage Pro guide have no seal-replacement section (barista-pro/shower-seal-not-documented)
How much descaler the Barista Pro needs: both booklets only say fill to the DESCALE line and add the descaling agent
Current US and UK names, SKUs and prices for Breville/Sage cleaning tablets, descaler, water filters and seals were not checked, so no accessory cards were created
Whether descaling actually restores weak steam is backed by one owner comment only; Breville lists scale as a cause of no steam, not weak steam

competitors.says: Breville's own Barista Express cleaning tutorial is a 1:20 video. It says the machine 'will notify you when to perform the next cleaning cycle', but the FAQ questions about a blinking or solid maintenance light show no answer text, and there is no schedule.

Breville's Barista Pro descale tutorial says the LCD will tell you when to descale and that minerals build up even with the filter in place. The steps are video-only, 'How often does Barista Pro need descaling?' is unanswered, and it isn't tied to the FLUSH cycle or daily care.

An owner thread where people contradict each other about whether the light means backflush or descale. One commenter states flashing = backflush and solid = descale, which matches the US manual. Nobody notes that UK Sage units label the light differently.

cardChanges.summary: Added maintenance claims from the US BES870 X26 booklet (light meaning, cleaning cycle, descale, symptoms, filter, daily care, seal replacement) and the UK Sage SES875 C21 quick guide (CLEAN ME light, no descale prompt, 60/90-day descale, filter 3 months/40 L), an owner report on the light confusion, and unknowns for maintenance intervals and the light's trigger/reset. No existing claims removed.
cardChanges.content:
# Barista Express

These claims were researched for the built-in grinder troubleshooter, the standalone-grinder guide and the clean/descale maintenance guide. The current US instruction booklet (BES870 USCM X26) was read page by page, including Care & Cleaning (pages 22-26) and Troubleshooting (pages 27-31). The UK Sage quick guide (SES875 UK C21) was read for Care & Cleaning (pages 15-18). The two markets label the maintenance light differently: the US panel has CLEAN / DESCALE, and the UK C21 guide has CLEAN ME and no descale prompt.

cardChanges.content:
# Barista Pro

These claims were researched for the built-in grinder troubleshooter, the standalone-grinder guide and the clean/descale maintenance guide. The current US instruction booklet (BES878 USCM Q26) was read page by page, including Care & Cleaning (pages 19–22) and Troubleshooting (pages 23–26). The Sage BES878/SES878 multilingual quick guide (UG5, Nov 2019) was read for Care & Cleaning (pages 18–21). The Pro has no maintenance light: its LCD shows FLUSH and DESCALE alerts.
